I oppose this increased dependence on technology because it adversely affects our ability to communicate meaningfully with others.

First, people are no longer going out to shop in person. When I lived in my home country, I regularly visited stores either by walking or riding my bike. However, after moving to the United States, this habit disappeared since my mother simply calls the store, and they deliver the products or food directly to us. This convenience eliminates valuable opportunities for face-to-face interaction with shopkeepers and other customers.

Second, friends are increasingly engaging with digital games rather than physical activities. Recently, I inquired with a friend back in my country about whether they still play soccer at local fields or other games in the streets. He informed me that they now prefer popular mobile games and have lost interest in traditional outdoor activities with friends.

Third, young children are becoming obsessed with digital devices at the expense of other developmental activities. My younger brother, who is just two years old, only wants to watch videos on a phone. When our mother takes the device away, he cries because he wants to continue watching videos or playing games rather than engaging with his surroundings or playing with other siblings.

Fourth, technology creates barriers during family visits and outings to new places. When I visit relatives, I find it difficult to put my phone away because I often feel disconnected or bored without digital stimulation. Similarly, when exploring new places, I tend to focus on taking photographs rather than fully experiencing the moment and connecting with the environment.

Some play games while others watch videos, deliberately sitting at the back of the room to avoid detection by teachers, even after being instructed to put their phones away. This behavior demonstrates how technology dependence can disrupt education and social norms.

Each time we fail, we gain experience and learn valuable lessons that contribute to eventual success.

He encountered countless failures, but rather than giving up, he confronted his challenges head-on.

This illustrates that maintaining optimism after setbacks isn't impossible, even for someone in difficult circumstances. While not everyone can do this effortlessly, we all desire happiness, and embracing failure can actually help us achieve it.

Ralph Waldo Emerson once stated that maintaining your authenticity in a society that constantly pressures you to conform represents life's greatest achievement. Despite differing opinions, I firmly support Emerson's perspective because society persistently attempts to mold individuals' viewpoints, cultural backgrounds, and belief systems.

Several compelling reasons support this viewpoint. Firstly, despite external pressures urging transformation, it's crucial to persist in being true to oneself. While some people might disapprove, the ultimate comfort comes from self-acceptance rather than external validation. Secondly, cultivating self-love and pride in one's identity is essential. Mistakes shouldn't define who we are; instead, they provide opportunities for growth. Every characteristic and personality trait contributes to what makes each person distinctively unique in a world that often encourages conformity. Thirdly, maintaining connection to one's cultural heritage is vital. When faced with expectations to assimilate and alter one's fundamental identity, the most significant achievement is demonstrating that you transcend others' limited expectations.

In conclusion, resist allowing the world to diminish your authenticity. Continue to persevere, value your intrinsic worth, and honor your background, as these elements collectively constitute your most remarkable accomplishment.

When we're born, we come out of our mother's womb, and the first thing we naturally do is screech and cry. If we don't cry, the doctor hits us on our backs and tries to make us cry. From that cry on, we develop our own kind of sound and our own screech with its own pitch. They take our fingerprints, which will never be the same as anyone else's, even when we're born with a twin. No matter how much alike we are, our fingerprints will never be identical. From there on, we start to learn and develop our own persona.

After we're born, our brain starts to function even in small ways. Babies learn to cry when they're hungry, when they need to be changed, when they're in pain, or simply when they want attention. When children get older into the toddler stage, they start to learn how to walk by observing everyone around them and learn to talk by listening to everyone else. We learn how to grab our bottle, pick up a fork or spoon, and practically master our own daily activities. But we learn all that from observing and listening to everyone else.

When we reach ages 6-12, we have a tendency to want to fit in and be part of the "cool kids" group. We watch TV and see celebrities in various professions: musicians, actors, painters, policemen, firemen, dentists, doctors, mayors, chefs, soccer players, basketball players, football players, baseball players, hockey players, tennis players, volleyball players, etc. The list could go on and on, but the point is that we are influenced by these examples. As we get older into our teen years (13-19), we start to develop our own voice—at least until we're old enough to make our own decisions. We all take our own paths and choose to make our own decisions. Our parents don't follow us around all day telling us what to do or not do or making every decision for us. They certainly give us plenty of advice because they've already been through that stage and don't want to see us fail and get hurt. But sometimes it's good that we fail and make mistakes because then we learn what we can and cannot do.

Now that you turn into an adult, that net we used to have while living under Mom and Dad's roof is no longer there—it's gone. We don't have that privilege anymore, and we need to grow up and create and develop our own persona officially. When we get a job, it comes with responsibilities, and from there we learn if we are responsible or irresponsible, social or non-social, lenient or non-lenient, patient or impatient, forgiving or unforgiving.

I'd like to think that we're all born to grow and learn about our rugged society, and based on what we've experienced is how we're going to act. We can literally live in a shit-hole of a place and have the happiest attitude ever—better than a boy or girl complaining that she didn't get the car she wanted. This compares to the kid who saw his mother get beaten by his deadbeat dad, or the kid who was up all night wondering if his mom was going to come home tonight, or even the kid who went to sleep hungry. So honestly, I don't think we're born with labels. I feel like we all can make our own decisions about what we're going to make of life—if we're going to sit there and make everyone see us as a pity case.

A huge part of your character is your mentality. If you have a broken-down, weak mindset, you're going to have negative vibes and a weak, deadbeat character. But if you have a strong mindset and the will to get things done, then you'll have a broad and respected character.

In conclusion, I'd like to think that we create and build our own character, and that we're not given a label by any higher power about what our character is going to be in life.

From the moment we enter this world emerging from our mother's womb, our first natural reaction is to cry out with a distinctive wail. In fact, if we don't cry immediately, medical professionals will gently stimulate us to ensure we do. This initial cry marks the beginning of our development of unique vocal characteristics with our own particular pitch and tone. Just as our fingerprints are completely unique to us, so too are our early vocalizations. Even identical twins, who may appear remarkably similar, develop their own distinct ways of expressing themselves from birth.

As we begin our journey of life, our minds start processing information from the very beginning. Infants quickly learn to communicate their needs through crying - whether they're hungry, uncomfortable, in pain, or simply seeking attention. When children progress into their toddler years, they acquire fundamental skills by observing those around them. They learn to walk by watching others walk, to speak by listening to conversations, and to perform daily activities like holding a bottle or using utensils by imitating adults.

During the elementary school years (ages 6-12), children often experience a strong desire to belong and be accepted by their peers. Through media exposure, they encounter numerous role models representing various professions and lifestyles - musicians, actors, artists, public servants, healthcare providers, athletes, and many more. These influences help shape their understanding of what's possible in life.

As teenagers enter their formative years (13-19), they begin to develop their own perspectives and voices. While their parents offer guidance based on their own life experiences and wish to spare their children from unnecessary pain and disappointment, young people must ultimately make their own decisions. Making mistakes and facing challenges, while sometimes difficult, provides valuable learning opportunities that help individuals understand their own capabilities and limitations.

Upon reaching adulthood, the safety net that once existed while living under parental supervision disappears. Adults must take full responsibility for their choices and actions. Employment brings with it various responsibilities that reveal aspects of one's character - whether someone is responsible or careless, social or reserved, patient or impatient, forgiving or judgmental.

I believe we're all born with the capacity to grow and learn within the complexities of society. The way we develop our character depends significantly on our life experiences. Someone raised in difficult circumstances might maintain a positive outlook, while another with material advantages might be perpetually discontent. Consider the child who didn't receive the desired birthday gift versus the one who witnessed domestic violence or went to bed hungry - their perspectives and character development will inevitably differ.

In my view, people aren't born with predetermined labels or fixed character traits. Each individual has the capacity to shape their own identity and determine their path in life. Our mindset plays a crucial role in this process. Those with a weak, defeated mentality tend to exhibit negative attitudes and develop diminished self-worth, whereas those with strong determination and a positive outlook tend to build respected, resilient characters.

In conclusion, I firmly believe that we create and develop our own characters throughout our lives. Rather than being assigned predetermined labels by any external authority, we have the power to shape who we become through our experiences, choices, and mental attitudes.

In my view, students require a period of rest following an extensive academic year, and this isn't merely beneficial for young people. We can observe similar needs in adults, who also require substantial breaks from their employment due to fatigue and work-related stress. Although I'm not equating students with adults—who carry greater life responsibilities—students' need for extra downtime and sufficient sleep is particularly understandable. Many professions provide only a week or two of vacation time (sometimes more), leaving employees feeling exhausted and wishing for longer breaks to enjoy with their families. The same principle applies to students who now have the opportunity for an extended vacation.

Furthermore, many students cherish summer for its warm breezes, seasonal atmosphere, and the sense of freedom it brings—freedom from grades, academic activities, and projects. This extended break makes a significant difference compared to shorter vacations. However, I also recognize educators' perspectives, as they might prefer not to review material from the previous year with students who have forgotten important concepts. That situation could certainly be stressful. But honestly, who wouldn't appreciate a longer vacation? For teachers who manage to save money, summer becomes especially enjoyable.

From a student's standpoint, I identify with the need for vacation time to relax. However, there's another compelling reason why breaks should remain as they are. Many students use summer to plan their goals, such as securing full-time employment (which even some teachers do) to save for college or other necessities. For many students, this represents a major objective, especially when they don't have the same level of financial support as their peers. At the same time, I understand that educators aim to help us achieve our goals, and the current schedule—one extended break of 3-4 weeks in summer, a longer winter break, and a week each in spring and fall—seems quite pleasant. Some students might actually prefer the weather during these other seasons, particularly autumn, so there's no issue with maintaining this arrangement.

In conclusion, the existing break duration is ideal because numerous students love it, the weather is pleasant, beaches are accessible, and there's sufficient time to visit family or travel. Additionally, it benefits those who wish to work during summer to earn extra money or help with their expenses.

The impact of technology on human interaction presents a complex picture with both advantages and disadvantages, and I believe this largely depends on individual circumstances.

On one hand, technology offers significant benefits for those who experience loneliness. Digital entertainment such as reading books, online shopping, gaming, streaming music through applications like Pandora, or watching favorite shows on platforms like YouTube and Netflix provides meaningful ways to spend time alone. This can be particularly valuable for individuals who might otherwise struggle with isolation. Furthermore, technology has revolutionized communication, making it easier than ever to connect with others. It delivers entertainment, keeps us informed about global events and even space exploration, and allows us to find information quickly without reading entire books. Everyday tasks have become more convenient too—we can shop from home and order food with just a few clicks.

However, technology also has drawbacks. With the prevalence of smartphones and other devices, people are gradually losing interest in traditional social activities. Family gatherings, for example, often see participants more focused on their screens than on meaningful interaction. Many people find it challenging to engage in simple conversations because others are frequently distracted by their phones, which can be perceived as disrespectful. This behavior might cause others to develop negative opinions about the person who is constantly checking their device.

Additionally, over-reliance on technology can foster laziness. People might wonder why they should perform tasks manually when their phones or computers can do it for them. This mindset could extend to personal relationships as well, with individuals preferring digital communication over face-to-face interaction. The danger lies in gradually replacing human connections with virtual ones, potentially leading to greater isolation over time.

In summary, technology represents a remarkable advancement that offers tremendous benefits when used appropriately. The key is to utilize technology as a tool rather than allowing it to dominate our lives or replace genuine human connection. Maintaining this balance is essential for preserving our social well-being in an increasingly digital world.

My uncle has in his wallet 100 dollars. He gave me 10 and kept the rest. I told him to save the money for tomorrow because he would need it. But he spent all the money to buy shirts, pants, and hats. The next day, he was asking for money for gas for the car. My uncle was happy to have the money and to buy things with it. He didn't listen when we told him he would need the money for tomorrow. He spent all the money on things that are good for him, but he knew he would need it tomorrow. He spent it all.

Seeking multiple opinions can help someone make a better choice. One of my friends had money in his packet. He said, "Let's go watch a movie at the cinema." But all the rest of us friends told him "no." The movie was already on CD and would cost much less to watch at home than at the cinema. When my friend received our opinions, we saw the situation from a different perspective than the one he was thinking from. Even though my friend wanted to watch the movie at the cinema, it would cost a lot of money to pay for it. That's how we told him to buy it instead.

When people ask for advice, they sometimes talk to more than one person. My dad gave me money to buy anything I want. Knowing that tomorrow I would need a white shirt, I bought a game instead. My dad told me about the place where we needed to go, and that I would need the shirt. Because of my obsession with the game, the next day I was asking if they could give me money to buy the shirt. My dad told me yesterday, "I told you to buy it, but you don't listen to me." Even though I knew about the shirt, this happened because I didn't listen. In addition, after all the talking and learning, I saved the money that day for this type of case.

The cases that happened, in summary, all talk about how important it is to listen to the people around you. All these situations happened because we didn't listen to the person next to us. And you, is it sometimes okay for more than one person to talk to you?

My uncle had $100 in his wallet, and he gave me $10 while keeping the rest. I advised him to save the money because he would need it the next day, but he ignored my suggestion and spent all of it on shirts, pants, and hats. As a result, the following day he had to ask for money to put gas in his car. My uncle felt happy about purchasing those items at the moment and didn't consider that the money would be needed for something more important the next day.

This situation illustrates why seeking multiple opinions can lead to better decisions. One of my friends wanted to use his money to watch a movie at the cinema, but the rest of us advised against it. We pointed out that the movie was already available on DVD for much less money. When my friend considered our perspectives, he realized that watching the movie at home would be more economical. Even though he initially preferred the cinema experience, he recognized the financial benefit of our suggestion.

People often consult multiple individuals before making important choices. My father gave me money to buy whatever I wanted, knowing I would need a white shirt for an upcoming event. Instead, I spent it on a video game. When I needed the shirt the next day and had to ask for more money, my father reminded me that he had suggested buying it earlier. Despite knowing about the shirt, my obsession with the game clouded my judgment. From this experience, I learned to save money for necessary purchases.

In summary, these examples demonstrate the importance of listening to advice from those around us. All these situations occurred because individuals failed to consider the perspectives of others. Don't you think it's beneficial to consult multiple people before making important decisions sometimes?

Some months later, his grades went down because, when I asked him where he was, he was doing something bad with his new friends. Then he became like one of them, and I think he didn't attend college. This is why I'm saying that to have a successful future, you have to be with people who will help you in your future.

I think we all agree on these three points: being a good person with everybody, having peace in your soul, and having a good connection with people around you. This makes me think about how important it is to have a good attitude, to show a good attitude to everybody, and to have a good attitude regardless of what is happening in your life.

I definitely agree that having a positive attitude is crucial for success. To build a fulfilling life, you must learn how to navigate challenges while showing the world your uniqueness. Being a kind person regardless of others' opinions or judgments is essential. When faced with difficulties, maintaining composure and approaching problems with a constructive mindset is vital because anger rarely leads to effective solutions. Therefore, treating everyone well, finding inner peace, and nurturing positive relationships with those around you are fundamental. You should respond to every situation with optimism, no matter what comes your way.

When you treat people kindly, you create a positive environment where everyone feels comfortable. This kindness is reciprocated, making you stand out in a world that sometimes seems negative. While many individuals may have poor attitudes, this shouldn't discourage you from remaining courteous. Instead, distance yourself from negative influences and seek out like-minded people who share your values. These connections will help you build a supportive community that contributes to your personal growth and achievement. For instance, I make an effort to be good to all people—my family, friends, and acquaintances. My friends are exceptional individuals whom I cherish, and they feel the same about me. This mutual respect developed because I took the time to understand their interests, habits, and aspirations. Importantly, they view me as someone with a positive outlook who contributes to their lives, and I want them in mine. I believe they will have bright futures because I recognize their potential for success.

Inner peace represents another crucial element of a meaningful life. From a place of tranquility, you can access positive emotions that bring comfort and stability. However, even when experiencing discomfort, it's important to cultivate peace. I understand this can be challenging, as a lack of inner peace can negatively impact various aspects of your life. To achieve peace, engage in activities you genuinely enjoy or find fulfilling pursuits that never become monotonous. Additionally, avoid becoming easily frustrated by minor issues, as allowing one problem to ruin your weekend or longer periods is counterproductive. Nothing compares to the value of inner peace. When I was twelve, my younger brother did something that upset me, and that negative feeling has remained with me. Now at twenty, I recognize that carrying this resentment isn't beneficial. While the memory occasionally resurfaces, I remind myself of my love for my brother and our close relationship. He's someone who listens to me and supports me, and when we talk, I experience a sense of peace.

Building strong connections with people around you significantly influences your attitude and future. Interacting with positive, goal-oriented individuals can shape your life direction constructively. These people know what they want in life and understand what might hinder their progress. Meeting such individuals is worthwhile—they are interesting to listen to, you can learn from them, and you can exchange ideas. Throughout your life, you'll encounter various people—some good, some bad. Some may invite you to socialize frequently or suggest fun activities, making you think they're beneficial for your success. However, truly valuable connections offer more than temporary enjoyment; they provide opportunities that positively impact your long-term future. Sometimes, those who seem to be limiting your fun might actually be helping you the most. I knew someone with great potential who excelled academically in earlier grades. However, in ninth grade, he began associating with students who performed poorly and lacked ambition. Several months later, his grades declined because he was engaging in negative activities with these new friends. Eventually, he transformed into one of them, and I doubt he attended college. This example illustrates why surrounding yourself with people who support your future aspirations is essential for achieving success.

After considering these three fundamental aspects—treating everyone well, finding inner peace, and maintaining positive connections—it becomes clear how important a good attitude is. Showing positivity to others regardless of your circumstances is key to building a successful and fulfilling life.

Technology has transformed how we complete everyday tasks, often without requiring face-to-face interaction. From borrowing books and shopping to gaming, digital solutions allow us to accomplish activities without direct human contact. This development has led to debates about whether technology's growing role in our lives brings more benefits or drawbacks. In my opinion, technology has significantly improved our quality of life by enabling long-distance communication, providing flexible work opportunities, and expanding our social and cultural understanding.

The primary benefit of technology is its ability to keep us connected with loved ones who are far away. Through video calls and messaging applications, we can maintain meaningful relationships regardless of geographical barriers. For example, family members separated by great distances can now share daily experiences and stay updated on each other's lives through regular digital communication. Without these technological tools, such connections would gradually weaken over time. Additionally, technology provides security during emergencies; when accidents occur, location services on smartphones can help family members find and assist quickly. Similarly, when health issues prevent us from going to work, technology allows us to inform employers promptly, something that would be challenging without modern communication methods.

Another advantage of technology is the opportunity to work remotely, eliminating the need for daily commutes. When working online, people save both time and money that would otherwise be spent on transportation. This flexibility proves particularly helpful for parents who wish to balance professional responsibilities with childcare. Furthermore, those unable to drive due to physical limitations can still pursue careers through remote work options. Technology also enables professionals to work while traveling, potentially increasing their income by taking on opportunities from different locations. This freedom to work from anywhere represents a significant improvement in work-life balance.

Technology also enhances our social experiences by making it easier to connect with new people and learn about different cultures. Social media platforms expose users to diverse perspectives from around the world, sparking curiosity about various traditions, languages, and lifestyles. This digital interaction often motivates people to learn directly by communicating with individuals from different backgrounds. When traveling to unfamiliar places, technology serves as an essential tool for navigation and communication. For instance, in foreign countries where language barriers exist, translation applications help overcome communication challenges, allowing travelers to ask for directions or seek assistance. These digital tools transform potentially stressful situations into manageable experiences.

In conclusion, technology has brought numerous positive changes to our lives. It keeps us connected with loved ones, offers flexible work opportunities, and expands our cultural understanding. Rather than reducing human interaction, technology enhances our ability to connect across distances and differences. When used thoughtfully, technology serves as a powerful tool that enriches our experiences in countless ways, making it an indispensable part of modern life.

In certain cultures, young people are often pressured to choose a career path before completing their secondary education. While early career planning can lead to focused educational journeys, students who commit to specific vocational tracks too soon may encounter difficulties. Many adolescents believe selecting a career at a young age offers advantages such as streamlined college preparation, smoother employment transitions, and reduced future decision-making stress. However, committing to a career prematurely presents significant drawbacks, including potential course abandonment, excessive anxiety about career choices, and inefficient use of valuable time.

First, students frequently abandon chosen career paths once they begin studying them. For example, many teenagers enroll in relevant classes but lose interest within just a few weeks of starting. This pattern often leads to diminished enthusiasm for their selected profession. When young people withdraw from these courses, they typically face challenges readjusting to other educational options. Consequently, thoughtful consideration before committing to a career path is essential.

Second, early career decisions create unnecessary mental pressure. Adults typically require considerable time to determine suitable career trajectories, and similarly, adolescents need space to explore possibilities. Young people often prioritize immediate employment opportunities because they desire financial independence. Additionally, maintaining social connections remains important during teenage years, with career planning naturally following once sufficient stability is achieved.

Third, premature career planning often results in wasted time. Young individuals frequently dedicate more time to leisure activities rather than serious career consideration. Many mistakenly believe careers are exclusively school-related, leading them to provide non-committal answers like "undecided" on planning documents. Instead, they often return to pursuing personal hobbies. Therefore, developing a structured approach before committing to career decisions is crucial.

Choosing a career at age twelve or younger represents an imprudent decision that generates undue stress, leads to abandoned pursuits, and creates negative associations with educational courses. Young people commonly abandon classes after just two or three weeks of participation. They frequently indicate uncertainty when asked about career intentions. While career development requires time, persistence is essential even when progress feels slow.

I firmly believe that honesty should be a fundamental principle in everyone's life. When I choose to be honest, I'm committed to speaking the truth and avoiding deception in my interactions with others. The value of honesty as the best policy stems from the fact that it enables others to place their trust in me, whether they're seeking my opinion or requesting assistance with their tasks. This trust remains valuable even when those around me may not always demonstrate the same level of integrity in their own actions.

Personally, I consider honesty to be the most essential quality in my character. As people mature and develop their thinking abilities, maintaining honesty throughout one's life becomes increasingly important. Another significant aspect of honesty in my experience is the confidence it provides - believing in my ability to succeed in academics or avoid negative situations like bullying.

However, I recognize that honesty doesn't always yield positive outcomes immediately. There might be instances when people become upset with me because they trusted my honest assessment, only to feel disappointed. In such situations, they might learn not to trust me in the future, which would be unfortunate. If I were to sacrifice honesty simply to make others happy while ignoring potential negative consequences, I would be doing a disservice to both myself and them.

Following a negative experience related to honesty with friends or family members, our relationship might be strained, and they might question my integrity. They could even seek out others they deem more reliable. Later in life, however, these same individuals might come to appreciate my honesty and reconcile with me. Our relationship could be restored, and we might develop a stronger understanding of each other's perspectives regarding honesty and its role in our connections.

What happens if they find multiple people to trust besides me? This could potentially lead to significant disagreements or even conflicts that might not easily resolve. It would be more productive to address these issues directly through face-to-face communication, ensuring that feelings aren't unnecessarily hurt and relationships aren't permanently damaged.

I find it valuable to surround myself with a community of honest individuals. Together, we can help our friends and family members overcome negative experiences with honesty and focus on building more positive relationships. This approach can reduce stress and prevent harmful thought patterns that might lead to serious mental health issues or self-destructive behaviors.

Even when others express distrust in my honesty, I don't allow it to lead to destructive thoughts about life or death. I will continue to advocate for honesty as a core value, even if I occasionally fail to meet my own standards. My commitment to honesty remains unwavering throughout my life.

For instance, if I'm concerned about failing an exam, my honest approach involves believing in my ability to succeed rather than anticipating failure. When I put forth genuine effort, I can trust in my own honesty and feel satisfied with the result. If I forget to study and subsequently perform poorly, the responsibility lies with my lack of preparation rather than with honesty itself. The mistakes I make on tests typically occur because I guessed answers rather than knowing them correctly.

Honesty serves as a valuable tool that I can rely on when needed to help me succeed and avoid failure in life. I believe everyone should prioritize honesty as a core personality trait because it can help resolve conflicts that might otherwise seem insurmountable. Many people initially disagree with the idea of always being honest, suggesting it shouldn't be their primary value. However, this perspective often comes from a misunderstanding of what true honesty means and how it contributes to personal success.

Some mistakenly believe that only highly intelligent people possess the best qualities of honesty. This view is incorrect. Honesty is equally valuable and achievable regardless of one's intelligence level. People who may not currently be considered bright can grow and develop their honesty over time, potentially gaining the support of others through their improved character. Similarly, intelligent individuals might maintain their growth or experience a decline in their intellectual capabilities. People might continue to trust these individuals even when their abilities diminish, especially if they begin to lie despite previously being known for truthfulness. This highlights the importance of guidance from family and teachers in reinforcing honest behavior, as friends might sometimes encourage dishonest tendencies.

When someone demonstrates genuine growth in honesty, friends and family members might be surprised by the transformation. They might wonder how the person changed and whether this development is permanent. Once they understand the nature of this change, they likely share this positive example with others. This illustrates why honesty deserves to be a top priority in everyone's life and why it represents the most beneficial approach to navigating relationships and personal development.

The human capacity to revise initial perceptions demonstrates that first impressions aren't fixed judgments. Many aspects of life reveal themselves differently upon closer examination, leading us to recognize that our initial reactions might not align with reality. This phenomenon explains why individuals frequently form negative opinions about people or situations without sufficient evidence.

Making conclusions based solely on first encounters can lead to significant errors in judgment. We often develop opinions about others before truly understanding their character or circumstances. What we initially perceive may not accurately reflect the truth, causing us to potentially overlook valuable connections or opportunities.

I personally experienced this lesson during my tenth grade year. I formed a negative opinion of a classmate, assuming he lacked respect for both peers and educators. This assumption prevented me from engaging with him despite sharing several classes. My goal was to avoid interaction, believing this would protect me from any negative behavior he might exhibit.

Over time, however, I discovered that this individual was actually one of the most trustworthy and kind people I had encountered. Our eventual friendship revealed that my initial assessment was completely incorrect. This experience taught me that with reflection and additional information, even strongly held first impressions can evolve and transform.

- Participants enjoy greater privacy and the freedom to create personalized study schedules
- Classes proceed without interruption from weather-related disruptions or other physical attendance barriers

Ralph Waldo Emerson once stated that "unless you attempt to accomplish something beyond your current capabilities, you will never experience growth." I fully support Emerson's perspective for several compelling reasons. Initially, I believe that when individuals fail to prepare themselves for multiple challenges and opportunities, their personal development stagnates. Secondly, possessing a diverse range of knowledge compared to others consistently provides a competitive edge. Finally, avoiding challenges that exceed our current expertise effectively halts our potential for advancement.

My primary rationale is that when people do not equip themselves with various skills and knowledge areas, their lives often lack direction and offer fewer possibilities in our society. This occurs because they lack the necessary expertise to secure quality employment. For instance, those seeking better job opportunities with new experiences will find it nearly impossible to attain such positions without the required qualifications. How can they contribute meaningfully to their country or community if they lack preparation for specialized roles that may be crucial?

Furthermore, when we develop multiple areas of expertise, our professional lives become significantly more flexible, enabling us to access better or more suitable employment opportunities. Knowledge represents one of the most powerful assets a person can possess. Some individuals mistakenly believe knowledge cannot be acquired or purchased. However, if one commits to continuous learning, they will consistently maintain an advantage for personal and professional growth. Ultimately, I contend that when people never attempt difficult challenges, their development remains limited. We must consistently pursue endeavors that introduce new experiences into our lives. Consider the example of someone who graduates with a teaching degree but remains content without pursuing more advanced positions like school administration—they will never reach their full potential.

In conclusion, I align with Emerson's assertion because his words provide specific insights into the nature of personal development. When he stated that "unless you try to do something beyond what you have already mastered, you will never grow," he captured an essential truth about human potential. This is why I endorse his perspective, as illustrated through the reasons I have presented.

With the advancement of educational approaches, schools have increasingly incorporated programs that nurture students' natural talents. These initiatives allow art-inclined students to explore their potential while providing a necessary break from academic pursuits. Such artistic engagements serve as a valuable opportunity for students to refresh their minds and regain energy for subsequent learning sessions. However, this approach may not be optimal for students who lack interest in artistic activities.

The contemporary high school experience often becomes monotonous for many students who struggle to identify their interests and passions within the academic framework. In this context, discovering enjoyable activities represents an effective strategy to counter this disengagement. Participating in creative pursuits like joining a musical band, engaging in drama productions, or attending art classes can significantly enhance students' motivation to learn. While these activities should be encouraged, they ideally remain voluntary choices rather than compulsory requirements.

Beyond stress relief, involvement in artistic disciplines facilitates mental clarity and improves information absorption capacity. Following intensive academic sessions, engaging in creative expression helps organize thoughts and prepares the mind for further learning. The effectiveness of this mental reset varies according to individual preferences, as different activities provide relaxation based on personal interests and inclinations.

While we advocate for students' participation in artistic classes, their elective nature remains crucial. Compulsory attendance would likely result in disengaged students disrupting the learning environment for genuinely interested participants. Such disruptions could manifest as inattentiveness or disruptive behavior, detracting from the positive experience for all involved.

In conclusion, art classes provide substantial benefits including stress reduction, improved cognitive function, and enhanced academic motivation. They create a more balanced and enjoyable educational experience. Nevertheless, maintaining these programs as electives ensures that participation remains among students who genuinely value and benefit from artistic engagement, maximizing both personal enjoyment and educational outcomes.

Ralph Waldo Emerson once remarked that unless we attempt to accomplish more than what we've already mastered, genuine growth cannot occur. This insightful observation emphasizes that true mastery means performing a task consistently and without mistakes. To advance ourselves, we must establish personal objectives. Even modest steps forward contribute significantly to our journey toward achieving more significant accomplishments. Not all skills are easily acquired; mastering them might require considerable time and effort, yet with proper self-assurance and determination, attainment becomes possible.

For instance, if you know how to ride a bicycle, challenge yourself by learning to operate a motorcycle. If baking cupcakes is within your abilities, progress to creating elaborate cakes. Similarly, if floating in water is comfortable for you, push yourself to become a proficient swimmer. These seemingly small challenges enhance existing capabilities and enable us to undertake more ambitious endeavors. Without actively stretching our current limits, we cannot hope to reach the objectives we set for ourselves. However, through persistent commitment, we can achieve our targets and transcend our existing knowledge base.

The inability to perform a particular task immediately should not deter anyone from eventual mastery. Continuous practice and perseverance are essential until proficiency is achieved. Otherwise, personal development remains stagnant. Ultimately, the choice rests with each individual: whether to embrace growth and strive toward life's goals or to remain static and never realize one's full potential.

Collaborative work versus independent effort

There are certainly advantages to teamwork, especially when you collaborate with people you enjoy and who possess the necessary skills. However, individual work offers greater benefits such as protecting your original ideas from being appropriated by others, which is a common occurrence when working in groups.

Group dynamics often result in unequal participation, where some members contribute less than others. This can create dependency and undermine personal confidence, making individuals feel they cannot accomplish tasks without assistance.

As a student, I've found that working alongside friends often leads to them copying my work, which frustrates me. It suggests they might struggle to succeed independently, which is concerning. It's disheartening when others benefit from group settings without actually putting in the required effort.

I personally prefer working alone rather than in teams. This isn't because I dislike social interaction; it's simply my preferred approach. When collaborating, I rarely feel I'm gaining anything valuable since others either cheat or don't contribute meaningfully. Working independently allows me to be my authentic self, persist without concerns about others, and accomplish more without needing external support.

Through my experiences, I've learned the importance of prioritizing oneself and having your own back. Based on my perspective, group work should generally be avoided because it shouldn't make you feel inadequate or dependent on others for validation or success.

The act of discovering an object on the ground and claiming it as your own constitutes a dishonest practice with significant ethical implications. When you encounter money, toys, or any personal belongings that have been discarded, you cannot be certain of their rightful owner. If someone later returns to search for their lost possession, they will be disappointed to find it absent because another individual has removed it. During my childhood, I frequently observed such situations and made it a point to either return items to their owners or inform them about what they had dropped.

Typically, when people encounter unattended items, their initial instinct might be to claim them for themselves. However, this approach is ill-advised because you have no way of knowing to whom the object belongs or its origin story. Possessing something that does not belong to you is fundamentally theft. Many individuals suggest leaving discovered items exactly where they were found, as owners often return to search for their lost belongings. It is uncommon for people to intentionally leave their possessions behind without awareness or concern.

Educational institutions frequently address this issue. In my elementary school, signs throughout the campus reminded students not to take items that weren't theirs and to leave found objects in their original locations. While many students adhered to these guidelines, some demonstrated disregard for others' property, which is unacceptable behavior. These individuals might not even have a genuine need for the item but simply desire to possess it. The distinction between need and want is crucial: need implies necessity or significant importance, where lacking the item would create hardship. If something is truly needed, it can typically be purchased from local retailers. Want, conversely, represents a desire that isn't essential—perhaps for showing off, entertainment, or mere acquisition despite no actual necessity.

When you discover something that isn't yours, refrain from taking it. If you witness someone dropping an item, return it to them. Be mindful of your actions, resist peer pressure, and strive to be both helpful and kind. This lesson carries substantial importance in contemporary society, where many individuals take without hesitation, and parental guidance sometimes falls short. Consequently, schools must intervene to educate young children about right and wrong.

Consider this scenario: you drop something valuable, like a favorite toy or an item you purchased with your own money. If you believe it's lost and someone else takes it, how would you feel? Likely, you would experience anger, sadness, or distress at the disappearance of something cherished. Now imagine the opposite: you drop your treasured possession, and someone immediately returns it to you. The emotions would likely shift to happiness, pride, or gratitude. This individual had no intention of keeping the item but recognized you as the rightful owner. You might have walked away completely unaware of your loss until needing the object later.

I personally experienced this when my iPad was taken years ago. The person who found it showed no regard for returning it. While I don't know who specifically took it, I was initially too preoccupied with other matters to notice. When I realized what had happened, I was extremely upset and had to rely on my mother's phone until my father purchased a new one for me.

This lesson is vital for demonstrating to children that taking what isn't theirs is both unwise and unnecessary. Many people don't consider the consequences until it happens to them. They might wonder why they became a victim of theft, failing to recognize that their own actions mirror those of the person who took their belongings—removing an item from where it was found, ensuring the owner never sees it again.

Some possessions hold substantial monetary value, particularly smartphones. People rely heavily on these devices, and any damage to them can cause significant frustration. Losing a phone would undoubtedly provoke anger, especially considering that modern smartphones often cost over $1,000, with some models exceeding this price point. When individuals lose their phones, they would typically search everywhere and go to great lengths to retrieve them, as these devices are essential for communication, safety, and assistance. If someone stole my phone, I would experience considerable anger and distress, knowing that replacing it would be challenging due to the high cost of new devices, which can sometimes approach the price of a used automobile.

I believe students would greatly benefit from the option to attend classes from home, as this approach would allow them to better prepare for learning and maintain greater focus throughout their sessions.

One significant advantage is that many students feel self-conscious at school due to peer pressure. For instance, some intelligent students hesitate to participate actively or speak up in class due to fear of judgment from others. However, when studying from home, these barriers are removed, enabling students to pursue their educational goals without the social constraints of a traditional school environment.

Consider a student who is alone at home with access to online resources. When encountering questions about their coursework, they develop self-reliance by seeking solutions independently. This approach to problem-solving builds valuable skills that extend beyond academics. Additionally, students can manage their personal needs more efficiently—such as preparing meals during breaks without disrupting their learning process. When questions arise, they can easily reach out to teachers through digital communication channels.

The flexibility of home-based learning would be particularly beneficial for students who experience social anxiety or require more individualized attention. Furthermore, students who prefer later study schedules could adjust their learning hours accordingly. This approach has proven valuable for pregnant students who often find traditional school settings challenging. A personal acquaintance shared her experience of continuing her education while pregnant and after childbirth. The ability to attend classes from home provided her with the comfort and flexibility needed to balance motherhood with her studies, something that would have been extremely difficult in a conventional school environment.

While I recognize the advantages of home-based learning, I also acknowledge potential challenges. Not all students have equal access to technology or reliable internet connections, which could create educational disparities. Additionally, some students might struggle with self-discipline when learning from home, potentially leading to procrastination or reduced academic performance. However, these obstacles can be mitigated through proper support systems and educational planning.

For students who need to work while studying, online learning offers a practical solution. They could structure their time to accommodate both employment and education, perhaps working some days and studying on others. This flexibility aligns with the principle that determination and consistent effort are essential for achieving academic success, even when facing challenging circumstances.

The benefits of attending classes from home become particularly evident during winter months when inclement weather might make commuting difficult. Students wouldn't need to worry about appropriate clothing or braving harsh conditions to attend school. Moreover, this learning environment eliminates potential conflicts with peers that might negatively impact a student's focus and emotional wellbeing.

Digital learning platforms can effectively deliver educational content through video conferences, providing clear explanations of complex concepts like mathematical problems. Students can utilize their devices to access information whenever needed, allowing for continuous learning throughout the day without the typical distractions found in traditional classrooms.

For students dealing with depression or other mental health challenges, the familiar and comfortable environment of home can significantly reduce stress and facilitate better learning outcomes. The absence of social pressures and the ability to learn at their own pace can contribute positively to their mental wellbeing.

In conclusion, while traditional schooling offers valuable social experiences, the option to attend classes from home provides numerous advantages that cater to diverse learning needs and personal circumstances. With proper support and resources, this approach can enhance educational outcomes while accommodating the unique challenges various students face.

Altering the school cafeteria menu would be an unwise decision for several reasons. Firstly, many students are selective eaters who might refuse to consume unfamiliar foods. When meals appear unappealing or have unusual aromas, students often choose to discard them or simply go without eating until they return home. This pickiness is quite common among young people who have specific standards about how their food should look and taste.

Secondly, schools may not be aware of all students' food allergies. Many children with dietary restrictions are hesitant to disclose their conditions due to fear of being teased by peers. Without this critical information, introducing new menu items could potentially trigger allergic reactions, creating serious health risks for vulnerable students.

Furthermore, changing menus represents a financial gamble for schools. Educational institutions invest resources in purchasing ingredients and preparing meals, only to have students reject the food and waste it. This financial loss could be better allocated toward other educational resources that would benefit the entire student body.

Ultimately, maintaining the current lunch menu represents the safest approach. It prevents potential health hazards, respects students' preferences, and allows schools to use their financial resources more effectively. By avoiding unnecessary changes, schools can ensure students remain well-fed and satisfied while preserving their budget for other essential needs.

The expectation that students should determine their career path prior to entering high school is a controversial issue. Many high schools design their curricula to steer students toward specific professional tracks from an early age. However, I believe pressuring adolescents to commit to a lifelong career at such a young age is inappropriate. Teenagers lack the maturity required to make such significant life decisions, which can lead to careless choices that don't serve their long-term interests.

One fundamental problem with this approach is that most high school students haven't gained sufficient exposure to various professions to understand which career might suit them best. Without real-world experience in different fields, young people cannot possibly make informed decisions about their future employment.

I personally believe this pressure comes too soon in one's educational journey. When I reach my junior and senior years, I plan to explore multiple career options before selecting courses that will best prepare me for my chosen path.

Additionally, adolescents are still developing and their interests often change. A student who chooses technology courses during freshman year might discover through research that this profession doesn't align with their expectations or financial goals, as happened to one of my friends who switched from technology classes to construction courses after learning more about both fields.

During these formative years, students should focus on academic responsibilities and personal growth rather than prematurely narrowing their options. The optimal time for making concrete career decisions arrives later, typically during senior year of high school or in college, when individuals possess greater self-awareness and life experience. At that point, selecting specialized courses that align with a well-considered career plan becomes more meaningful and beneficial.

I support Emerson's perspective because possessing expertise in a field enables superior performance in related tasks. Individuals with specialized knowledge gain access to superior opportunities and secure more prestigious positions compared to those lacking such qualifications.

However, not everyone shares this viewpoint. Some contend that occasionally, individuals without formal mastery may outperform those with qualifications in certain job contexts.

For instance, in a restaurant setting, a chef who has mastered culinary techniques only needs to recall recipes, whereas others must memorize various ingredients, tools, and equipment operations.

Second, expertise provides enhanced opportunities since credentials demonstrate your preparedness for specific roles. For example, many companies require candidates to possess advanced qualifications for particular positions. Similarly, upscale restaurants often mandate managerial degrees for supervisory roles, which typically come with higher compensation.

Third, individuals with expertise attain superior positions compared to those without such qualifications due to their demonstrated experience. For instance, if a restaurant needs to hire for kitchen roles, management positions, and dishwashing duties, someone with qualifications would likely be considered for the managerial post. Those without formal training would probably be assigned to dishwashing, and advancing to management would require significantly more time and effort.

In conclusion, people with expertise enjoy better opportunities, perform tasks more effectively, and secure more favorable positions than individuals without such qualifications. Therefore, I concur with Emerson's assertion that without mastery, personal and professional growth remains limited.

But at least teachers can show students the right way to get achievements or achieve their goals. That would be enough, and students will start thinking about how to get achievements and then they'll probably start working on their self-confidence and self-esteem.

In addition, when I came to the United States in 2017, I didn't know any English and had no friends at school. Everyone knows how hard it is to go to school without being able to speak with anyone or have friends, especially when you're a shy person like I was.

When someone tried to talk to me, my face would turn red and I would start blushing. It was all because I didn't have self-confidence.

So, I am still trying my very best to learn the language and make friends at school so I can play or do my work with them.

That being said, now I can speak, write, and read very well. I have become much more confident, the best version of myself, have many friends, and am happy to attend school.

Overall, being self-confident and working hard for achievements is like a key for building students' self-esteem, which comes from achievements.

Students should focus at school or wherever else they study so they get achievements, which helps them build their self-esteem.

Students also should be encouraged by their parents to build their self-esteem, as well as by themselves unless they are self-confident in life.

I believe that genuine self-esteem stems from accomplishments because when students dedicate themselves to their studies, they naturally accumulate more successes. As they earn recognition and achieve their goals, they develop a sense of pride that forms the foundation of true self-esteem.

Many students diligently complete their assignments on time and even balance part-time jobs, yet struggle to build authentic self-esteem. These individuals need to focus on developing self-confidence first, as it serves as the prerequisite for establishing meaningful self-worth.

Conversely, some students possess natural self-confidence despite having fewer commitments outside school, yet they lack understanding of how to translate this into genuine self-esteem through achievements.

Therefore, students should strive for excellence in their academic pursuits, as accomplishments serve as powerful motivators that foster self-esteem development.

Self-esteem can be cultivated independently by students who apply themselves diligently, maintain punctuality, and organize their responsibilities through structured planning tools like calendars.

I've observed that many contemporary students seem to lack dedication in their studies. Whether this stems from technological distractions or other factors, the result is the same—they fail to pursue meaningful academic achievements.

What disheartens me is witnessing these students' potential going unrealized. If they would simply dedicate a couple of hours each day to their studies, they would undoubtedly experience greater academic success and move closer to achieving their aspirations.

Thus, the path to authentic self-esteem begins with pursuing achievements and developing self-confidence, ultimately enabling students to become their best selves.

Educators also play a significant role in this process. Considering students typically spend more time with teachers than parents during weekdays, instructors have substantial influence. While teachers shouldn't directly discuss self-esteem with students unless specifically asked, they can guide them toward effective goal achievement strategies. This indirect approach often inspires students to independently develop their confidence and self-perception.

When I first arrived in the United States in 2017, I faced similar challenges. With limited English proficiency and no friends, school became an intimidating environment. My extreme shyness caused me to blush whenever someone approached me, a clear indication of my lack of self-confidence.

Nevertheless, I persisted in improving my language skills and forming friendships. Today, I communicate effectively in English, have numerous friends, attend school enthusiastically, and have developed a much greater sense of confidence. This personal journey demonstrates how dedicated effort leads to achievement and, ultimately, self-esteem.

In conclusion, self-confidence combined with diligent pursuit of achievements forms the essential key to developing self-esteem in students. Educational institutions should emphasize the importance of focused effort to help students accumulate achievements that contribute to their self-perception and personal development.

Thomas Jefferson once stated that "it is wonderful how much may be done if we are doing." This quote raises an important question: should we constantly pursue activities, or does inactivity also have value? Some argue that occasional rest serves a purpose by allowing us to recharge and maintain our capacity for work. However, others believe that continuous effort leads to greater achievements and benefits society as a whole.

Every day, millions of people rise to work diligently, giving their best in their chosen fields. But what about those unable to find traditional employment? Even without a conventional job, individuals can contribute to society or focus on personal development. Volunteering or helping others are meaningful ways to remain active. While everyone needs rest, excessive idleness can prevent us from realizing our aspirations and objectives.

Consistently engaging in worthwhile activities proves beneficial when approached with dedication and passion. Every worker has motivations—whether it's achieving personal goals, supporting loved ones, or simply enjoying the satisfaction of productive labor. As my mother often reminds me, if you desire something, you must pursue it actively. We all deserve better futures, which is why maintaining momentum in life matters.

From a societal perspective, participation is essential regardless of whether you have specific ambitions. Basic necessities like food, shelter, and utilities require employment. Beyond paid work, contributing through community service fosters personal growth. Whether compensated or voluntary, activities that make us feel productive and valuable to society tend to be inherently rewarding.

Humanity progresses through active engagement. Dreams and ambitions drive people to take meaningful action. Consider how your level of productivity—whether consistently active or occasionally inactive—shapes your life's direction. Jefferson's timeless quote invites us to reflect on our choices and purpose in life. While brief respites are healthy, we must remember that goals and dreams require persistent effort to become reality.

To the City Council,

I believe implementing a curfew for teenagers would be beneficial as it would help prevent them from engaging in problematic activities. There are certain young individuals who remain outdoors specifically to cause disturbances to the community. It would be advantageous to require teenagers to return home by 10 PM, as those on the streets during late hours are more likely to get involved in mischief and bother others. Additionally, students who need adequate rest for their education would benefit from this regulation, as they would have proper time to sleep before attending school classes. If such a curfew were established, authorities should create legislation stating that any teenager found outdoors past 10 PM would be violating the law.

Many adolescents find themselves in detention centers because of activities they should not participate in. Some possess firearms, even though many are not yet eighteen years old, which is against regulations. Others are incarcerated without valid reasons, often associating with peers who carry weapons or engage in other unlawful activities. Not all weapons discovered actually belong to the teenagers; some are found in bodies of water where others discarded them, and the previous owner's actions become attributed to the person who found the item. The City Council's proposal for a curfew aims to protect young people by keeping them away from potential trouble.

Although some argue that a curfew restricts personal freedom, looking at the situation from another perspective, while it does limit teenagers' nighttime activities, those limitations exist because some young people engage in harmful behavior. The curfew is ultimately designed to assist them.

In conclusion, I strongly support keeping teenagers off the streets after 10 PM, as this measure would effectively reduce their likelihood of encountering or causing problems.

A four-day school week means forgetting about the fifth day of school. Instead of coming for a short time on five days, students would use the full time on four days.

The concept of implementing a four-day school week has sparked considerable debate regarding its advantages and drawbacks. Rather than maintaining the conventional five-day schedule, educational institutions should transition to a four-day model for numerous compelling reasons.

By reducing the school week to four days, we lose ten instructional hours weekly. However, this can be compensated by extending each school day by two hours, allowing for more comprehensive class sessions. This additional time enables students to complete assignments and projects in class, reducing homework stress. Moreover, the extended schedule provides more opportunities for students to interact with teachers, particularly those who require extra help to succeed academically.

The fourth day, with its extended hours, could be dedicated to specialized activities such as library time for avid readers, sports participation, or other extracurricular pursuits. This flexibility caters to diverse student interests and learning styles.

The resulting three-day weekend offers numerous benefits. Students can use one of these days for medical appointments, eliminating the need to miss regular class time and the common practice of submitting absence notes. This approach would minimize classroom disruptions and improve attendance rates.

Teachers, many of whom are also parents, would appreciate an additional day to spend with their families and manage personal responsibilities. For seniors navigating the crucial decisions about higher education and potential weekend employment, the extra time is invaluable. Similarly, freshmen transitioning from middle school require adjustment time to adapt to high school routines.

The extended weekend could also facilitate community service opportunities, with proper parental consent and adult supervision. Students might participate in environmental cleanup initiatives or other community projects. Additionally, schools could partner with businesses to create programs connecting students with part-time employment opportunities during these free days.

While the extended school day might concern students with part-time jobs, the overall schedule actually provides more flexibility. Working students could potentially secure full-time positions on their day off and maintain weekend employment. Furthermore, despite longer school days, students would have additional free days for rest, homework completion, and personal pursuits.

Although there are valid concerns to address, the benefits of a four-day school week outweigh the drawbacks for the vast majority of students. Everyone deserves a three-day break from school obligations. Whether students choose to use this time for family activities, household responsibilities, employment, or personal study, the flexibility is universally beneficial. By collectively advocating for this change, students can work together to secure this new educational right that would benefit high school and college communities alike.

Some people argue that students should be required to take classes in the arts or other elective subjects. Consider the experience of discovering something that brings you joy and allows you to explore your capabilities. Many believe that mandatory electives in schools can help students identify their interests, develop valuable skills, and seize opportunities, ultimately benefiting them in their future endeavors.

It's crucial that students have some autonomy in selecting their electives. Picture a scenario where students are forced into classes they have no interest in. This would likely lead to disengagement, causing students to skip classes. When students miss classes, their academic performance suffers, leading to frustration and diminished motivation. Consequently, some may give up entirely, risking their ability to accumulate enough credits for graduation. Without a high school diploma, students face barriers to college admission and better employment opportunities. In severe cases, individuals without proper education may struggle with homelessness and other life hardships. This is why it's essential that students have a say in which electives they pursue.

Many people believe that every individual possesses unique talents. Students should explore electives where they can discover and hone their strengths. When students excel in a particular subject, they naturally develop a passion for attending class, which results in better grades and a desire to learn more. Additionally, they earn credits while developing skills that create numerous life opportunities. Individuals with diverse skill sets are often highly sought after by employers. For instance, a talented drama student might be cast in a film production, potentially leading to fame and financial success. Moreover, students aren't limited to developing just one skill—they can cultivate multiple abilities. This breadth of experience and knowledge significantly enhances their prospects. One compelling reason for students to identify and develop their skills is the multiplier effect it has on their future options.

The future is particularly important for students, and electives play a vital role in preparing them. When students engage with electives they genuinely enjoy and excel at, they're more likely to leverage these experiences to build a promising future after high school, including during their college years when adulthood truly begins. This is why it's crucial for students to identify and develop their skills—to ensure their future is manageable rather than overwhelming. While there will undoubtedly be challenges and difficult times, these acquired skills will help them navigate obstacles. This is also the stage where students begin to pursue their dreams, utilizing their abilities to create better futures. With clear direction and understanding, students can find their true calling and the destination they wish to reach.

However, some might argue that requiring electives is unnecessary because students lack sufficient motivation to engage with them seriously and may treat these classes as a joke rather than valuable learning opportunities.

Summer assignments often require students to continue their education during break, but an important question arises: should these projects be designed by teachers or students? I firmly believe that students should take the lead in creating their own summer projects.

Students possess a clear understanding of their own academic strengths and weaknesses. When they develop their own projects, they can focus specifically on areas where they need improvement. This approach allows them to maintain their learning momentum during the break while developing valuable skills through self-directed practice. By the time school resumes, they will have a stronger foundation because they've been working on material they chose themselves.

The first advantage of student-designed projects is comfort and familiarity. When students create their own assignments, they fully understand the topic and requirements, making the work process smoother and more natural. This familiarity reduces anxiety and increases the likelihood of successful completion.

Secondly, personalized summer projects help prevent knowledge loss. When students continue working on subjects they've chosen, they're more likely to maintain their academic progress. Without this self-directed learning, students might become complacent and forget important concepts. For instance, language learners who create their own summer practice activities are less likely to lose their skills compared to those who don't engage in any structured learning.

In conclusion, student-designed summer projects offer significant benefits. They allow young learners to work on areas they identify as important, prevent summer learning loss, and promote independence. Students demonstrate greater initiative and showcase their abilities when given the freedom to design their own educational experiences. The evidence clearly supports empowering students to create their own summer projects.

Ralph Waldo Emerson once stated, "To be yourself in a world that is constantly trying to make you something else is the greatest accomplishment." The actions, behaviors, and approach we take in our daily lives demonstrate our true character and value to the world. In many societies worldwide, people often view going beyond one's assigned duties as a sign of humility. For instance, in your professional environment, academic setting, or community, taking on tasks that aren't necessarily your responsibility reveals a generous spirit and shows the world that you're willing to make a positive difference. I strongly agree with this viewpoint because when you remain true to yourself, others notice something unique about you and may seek to emulate you. While initial attempts might not yield perfect results, persistence in maintaining your authentic self amid conformity is admirable.

There are three primary reasons why being yourself is essential. First, others are likely to follow your example. When you consistently go the extra mile, such as helping a classmate with mathematical problems outside your classroom duties, people take notice. While the teacher holds primary responsibility for instruction, your willingness to assist demonstrates character that many will want to mirror.

Second, being yourself allows you to become an inspiration to others across various environments - at home, in your neighborhood, at school, in college, and even within religious communities. For example, when neighbors see you maintaining your property well or assisting others by cutting grass or offering help, they may feel motivated to do the same. This represents the accomplishment of becoming a source of motivation for those around you.

Third, your achievements can transform the thinking of people in your circle. When they observe your progress in life, they may wonder, "How did they manage that?" You can share your journey and explain that if you succeeded, they might be able to as well. Within families, for instance, we often observe different dynamics - some members work low-paying jobs while others run their own businesses. By being the type of person who actively supports your family, you transmit positive energy, hope, and encouragement to your relatives.

In conclusion, as Emerson suggested, humans continuously strive to exceed expectations in order to achieve meaningful results and accomplishments in life. The majority of people worldwide recognize the benefits of helping others and perceive the positive message in Emerson's words. By consistently going beyond what is required, we create examples for those around us. More than serving as mere examples, we can become inspirational figures who motivate numerous individuals across the globe.
